SHW.rationale: Sherwin-Williams is a durable quality compounder with a dominant distribution moat (69.4% U.S. Paint Stores share), demonstrated pricing power (5% Jan 2025 increase, 7% planned Jan 2026), and consistent shareholder returns (47 consecutive dividend years). Q1 2026 results confirmed the franchise is intact: revenue +6.8% YoY, EPS +7.5% YoY, gross margin stable at ~49%, and adjusted EPS of $2.35 beat consensus of $2.28. The PE has compressed to 30.7x, near its 12-month floor of 29.4x (range 29.4–37.1), representing ~16% multiple compression from the peak — more than justified by modest margin normalization (net margin 11.6% → 10.9%, ROE 64.9% → 58.7%) but potentially overshooting given the franchise's resilience. The BPA ban in European packaging coatings (effective Q2 2026) provides a dated, fundamental near-term catalyst for incremental revenue. However, the case is tempered by: (1) WTI crude at $108.64/bbl (+76.4% over lookback) creating material input-cost risk that may not yet be fully reflected in margins, (2) earnings yield of 3.3% sitting 110bp below the 10-year Treasury, leaving limited margin of safety, (3) management's own guidance of only ~2.4% adjusted EPS growth at midpoint for FY2026, and (4) a softer demand environment with DIY weakness and muted construction activity. The stock is mildly attractive — a quality franchise at a fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation relative to its own history, with a modest near-term catalyst, but not yet cheap enough to be compelling given the macro headwinds.

Pricing power demonstrated: 5% increase Jan 2025, 7% planned Jan 2026, with low-single-digit volume growth maintained
BPA ban in European packaging coatings effective Q2 2026 — management called it a 'nice tailwind' with customer conversions through 2027
WTI crude at $108.64/bbl (+76.4% over lookback) — primary input-cost risk; management raised raw material inflation outlook to low-to-mid single digits
Earnings yield 3.3% vs 10-year Treasury 4.4% — negative equity risk premium of -110bp limits margin of safety
FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance $11.50-$11.90, implying only ~2.4% growth at midpoint
ROE compressed from 64.9% to 58.7%, net margin from 11.6% to 10.9% — modest but real deterioration justifying some de-rating
Leverage: total debt $11.7B, net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA 2.5x, interest expense +26.8% YoY
